newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SAQLAIN SPINS SURREY TO EARLY WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SAQLAIN SPINS SURREY TO EARLY WIN.

text.p: Surrey's Pakistani off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq, who took a hat-trick on Friday, completed match figures of 10 for 116 on Sunday to consign Middlesex to an innings defeat on the third day of their four-ay English county championship match.

One of his victims was Mark Ramprakash, who celebrated his recall to the England team for the sixth test against Australia with a second ball duck as Middlesex tumbled to 201 all out to go down by an innings and 125 runs.
Yorkshire's new left-arm paceman Paul Hutchison completed his first-innings demolition of Hampshire to help enforce the follow-on, before a Hants fightback threatened to restore the balance.
Hutchison added the wicket of Lee Savident to his overnight haul to claim seven for 50 as Hampshire were bowled out for 281 in reply to Yorkshire's 501.
But Jason Laney (81) led a stiffer Hants second innings which ended the day on 173 for three, still 47 runs behind.
Nottinghamshire milked 125 runs for their last four wickets to reach 356 all out and a 19-run first-innings lead against Somerset.
In reply, Somerset were 248 for four by the close.
Gloucestershire finished on 271 for six by the close against Sussex.
Earlier, Sussex's last three wickets realised 106, an eighth-wicket stand between wicketkeeper-captain Peter Moores (65) and young off-spinner Justin Bates (47) accounting for 104 of them.

Captain Matthew Maynard's unbeaten 161 and 46 from No 10 Waqar Younis could not achieve parity for Glamorgan against Worcestershire as Philip Weston (106 not out) promptly set about increasing an already handy first-innings lead of 78.
After Maneer Mirza (three for 95) had picked up two quick wickets to finish Glamorgan off for 398 in the morning Worcestershire reached 263 for seven and a healthy overall lead.
On Saturday Derbyshire beat Lancahire by an innings and 37 runs.
